steps.text: Stir mayonnaise, sugar, milk, buttermilk, lemon juice, vinegar, salt, and pepper together in a bowl until smooth.
Combine coleslaw mix and onion in a large bowl. Pour mayonnaise mixture over top and stir until well combined. Chill for 1 hour before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Restaurant-Style Coleslaw
raw_recipe.description: This coleslaw recipe makes creamy coleslaw with a sweet-tart taste. The dressing is made with buttermilk, mayonnaise, lemon juice, and vinegar.
raw_recipe.name: Restaurant-Style Coleslaw

review.reviewBody: Nothing could be quicker than this and so much better than store bought. The one thing I find with store bought is it's just too sweet - you can control the sweetness yourself with this one. I didn't cut back on the sugar the first time and found it a tad too sweet - so I added some dry powdered mustard and more black pepper to overcome that. I also used all buttermilk (making my own out of 1/2 cup milk - l/2 tablespoon of white vinegar - let sit for 10 minutes). By the way - the longer your coleslaw sits the runnier it will get because the cabbage leaks out water when it is mixed with the dressing - which is a good thing - you are getting the taste of cabbage. The longer it sits the more flavorful it becomes. I always try to make coleslaw way in advance (as much as three days). You can always transfer it to another bowl before serving to get rid of the excess juices if you like. My fellow cooks - think about it - do you think that KFC and stores are preparing their slaw one hour before our purchase??? Thanks submitter - its a keeper and really nothing has to be changed - my minor change of now just using a tad less sugar and all buttermilk is just a matter of preferance.

This recipe is a GREAT one! I have made it many times. I found a similar recipe in a cookbook by Todd Wilbur (Top Secret Recipes). In the cookbook this recipe calls for 8 cups chopped cabbage and 1/4 cup shredded carrots, everything else is the same. This may help if you are making your own mix. He also states to make sure to let cole slaw sit at least two hours before serving. Happy Cooking!!
I been making this for years. I only add some of the sauce at the beginning & save the rest. This keeps the slaw from being too runny. I add more sauce as needed.

Here's my 25 cents: first of all - made day in advance. I happened to find a really small inner head of cabbage (1 lb) and used my Moulinex to shred it along w/the carrot. I had a bit over 4 cups of cabbage, but I used entire dressing amounts. I guess because I had shredded the majority of inside of a cabbage, I didn't get much drainage of juice after salting...so...I rinsed it and let it dry on a tea towel. Anyway...I didn't use plain milk at all, only buttermilk. I did use suggestion by DIZ re: added a tsp of olive oil and whipped up dressing with immersion blender. Next day my slaw was very 'tight' so I added enough milk to loosen it up a bit. I did add celery seed and onion powder as well. At first taste it wasn't anything special but next day it was just what I was looking for. I did reduce sugar slightly (personal pref). I usually make coleslaw for pulled pork or BBQ chicken sandwiches so I don't need large amounts. 1/2 the slaw with entire amounts for dressing worked out perfectly for me. Not hard to tweak for personal tastes but really needs time to marinate for best flavor. I like it!

I doubled this recipe for a big family. I omitted the buttermilk, milk and vinegar. I used whole greek yogurt to replace all those. Added another TBSP of lemon juice for a bit more tang. I also did not use bagged slaw mix and opted to chopped my own green, red cabbage, and shredded my carrots with a veggie peeler followed by a rough chop. We prefer the chunkier version. I also added bit more onion, personal preference. IT IS DELICIOUS!!!!! Variation is to add in some dried less sugar cranberries, or even match stick apples also delicious.

This recipe deserves 4 stars because it gave me a great starting point for my coleslaw. Upon reading a lot of reviews I decided the recipe might not be perfect for me so I modified it a little bit. Hope this is helpful for those of you who prefer a creamier coleslaw (that does not get too watery over time). I also reduced the recipe to 4 servings. 

The first thing I did a couple hours before I wanted to make the coleslaw was to salt it with table salt to help extract some of the moisture out of the coleslaw (do this in a strainer). When I was ready to make the coleslaw I patted it dry and put it to the side. Next I mixed the following ingredients together to make the dressing: I omitted the onion (optional), and added 1/4 cup mayo, 2 splashes (I eye balled it) of milk, 2 tablespoons of sour cream, 1 teaspoon of white wine vinegar, 1.5-2 teaspoons of lemon juice, ground black pepper, and about 2 tablespoons of sugar (I did not add more salt since I salted the coleslaw in the first step). Feel free to give the dressing a taste and make changes as needed. Mix the coleslaw and dressing and let it sit in the refrigerator for an hour. Delicious!
I doubled the amounts for onion and sauce. I added half to the slaw and saved the rest for an amazingly versatile dressing! Wow. I love this stuff!

I loved this slaw. Did not use any milk at all as I knew it would be too soupy. I also made it in batches so that the coleslaw was crunchy for my BBQ pulled pork sandwiches. While tossing the dressing in with the cabbage mix I would then sprinkle celery seed in to it. I quadrupled this recipe as I was feeding 50. Perfect amount. Added an extra cup of mayo (Best Foods) to the sauce recipe and it was pertect. As the slaw sat it would juice up which is normal. Glad I didn't use any milk or buttermilk. Will be making this again. Flavor is spot on!
I love this recipe. the only thing I do differently is, once the dressing is poured over the coleslaw, I mix it up with my hands, squeezing the cabbage for about 2 minutes.

I've tried all kinds of recipes for slaw to serve with pork bbq, and glad I finally found this one! Didn't have buttermilk, but subbed with half-and-half with a little bit of cider vinegar. Worked perfectly, and the slaw was really good, with restaurant-quality taste. Thank you for this one!

I made this using the suggestion of creating buttermilk by taking 1/2 cup regular milk and mixing it with 2 Tablespoons vinegar and 3 tablespoons lemon juice. The dressing was so good but I only used half of it to keep it from being runny. I also used frozen chopped onion and that worked out well.

This ia a fantastic recipe. Love it just how it is. However, I have had to change my eating, so huge carb cuts. I make the recipe slightly different to stay on a Healthy Keto. I use 1/2 cup heavy cream instead of the milks. I use apple cider vinegar instead of white. And I use 1/8tsp of organic Stevia instead of sugar. SO good!!! Either way this is some of the bet coleslaw out there!
I only use a tablespoon of lemon juice
I cut it in half for the two of us. The only thing I added was some diced bell pepper. Otherwise exactly as written. The buttermilk adds just the right tang. Loved it.
easy and good
Easy and fast, taste delicious.

Very good and tasty cole slaw!! Not too many seasonings, not too wet, but still great flavor! Definitely recommend for anyone who doesn't like their cole slaw drowning in liquid, but I honestly wouldn't have minded a little more liquid, it depends on personal preference!
Perfect, especially with the added cayenne pepper! Love it,
Just what I was looking for. Simple, easy to put together. Everyone loved it. There you are!
